sentences.en: This is the 99% Invisible Breakdown of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 这是《99%隐形》对宪法的深度解析。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And I'm Elizabeth Chapp.
sentences.zh: 我是伊丽莎白·查普。

sentences.en: Today, we're covering Article 1 of the Constitution, which established the legislative branch of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要探讨宪法第一条，它确立了联邦政府的立法分支。

sentences.en: And our guest for our discussion is a member of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的嘉宾是美国众议院议员，

sentences.en: House of Representatives, Sharice Davids.
sentences.zh: 莎丽丝·戴维斯。

sentences.en: Representative Davids has served Kansas' third congressional district since 2019.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯议员自2019年起一直代表堪萨斯州第三国会选区。

sentences.en: She is one of the first two Native American women elected to the United States Congress, along with Deb Haaland from New Mexico, who was elected in the same year.
sentences.zh: 她是美国国会首批当选的两名美洲原住民女性之一，另一位是同年当选的来自新墨西哥州的黛布·哈兰德。

sentences.en: She was raised by a single mother.
sentences.zh: 她是由单亲母亲抚养长大的。

sentences.en: She is a first-generation college student.
sentences.zh: 她是第一代大学生。

sentences.en: She put herself through school.
sentences.zh: 她靠自己完成了学业。

sentences.en: She eventually graduated from Cornell Law School.
sentences.zh: 最终她从康奈尔大学法学院毕业。

sentences.en: When people learn about her, they can't help but mention that she was a professional, promising MMA fighter for a short period of time.
sentences.zh: 当人们了解她时，总会提到她曾有过一段职业综合格斗（MMA）选手的经历，表现非常出色。

sentences.en: I can't seem to resist it either.
sentences.zh: 我也忍不住要提一下。

sentences.en: It's awesome.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: If I was invited to a party with everyone in the House of Representatives, I would make a beeline to Representative Davids and talk about infrastructure with her all night long.
sentences.zh: 如果我受邀参加众议院所有成员的聚会，我会径直走向戴维斯议员，和她聊上一整晚的基础设施建设。

sentences.en: She's very into infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 她对基础设施非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And it turns out she's extremely into the processes and procedures of getting things done in Congress, the hidden aspects of Article 1.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，她对国会办事的流程和程序，也就是宪法第一条中那些隐秘的方面，有着极大的热情。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's one of the reasons why we invited her as our book club gueSt.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们邀请她作为读书会嘉宾的原因之一。

sentences.en: Representative Sharice Davids, thank you so much for being on the 99% Invisible Breakdown of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 莎丽丝·戴维斯议员，非常感谢您参加《99%隐形》的宪法解析节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

sentences.en: So we're covering Article 1 of the Constitution, and we're kind of dividing our discussion roughly into two parts, with today's discussion centering on the first half of Article 1.
sentences.zh: 我们正在讨论宪法第一条，我们将讨论大致分为两部分，今天主要集中在第一条的前半部分。

sentences.en: So, Elizabeth Cho, do you want to give us a summary of Article 1?
sentences.zh: 那么，伊丽莎白·乔，你想给我们总结一下第一条吗？

sentences.en: What is it all about?
sentences.zh: 它主要讲了什么？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Here goes.
sentences.zh: 开始了。

sentences.en: Article 1 is all about Congress.
sentences.zh: 第一条讲的都是国会。

sentences.en: The most important part is right at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 最重要的一点就在开头。

sentences.en: And Section 1 says, all legislative powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States, which shall consist of a Senate and House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 第一款规定，本宪法授予的全部立法权，应属于由参议院和众议院组成的合众国国会。

sentences.en: So basically, this first part of Article 1 gives or vests the federal government's lawmaking power to a representative body of two houses, the House and the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，第一条的这一部分将联邦政府的立法权授予了一个由众议院和参议院组成的代表机构。

sentences.en: And the herein granted part of Section 1 means that Congress can only use power that is specifically given to it in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 而第一款中“授予的”这一表述意味着，国会只能行使宪法明确赋予它的权力。

sentences.en: So that's not like, say, the state legislatures of California or Kansas.
sentences.zh: 这与加利福尼亚州或堪萨斯州的州议会不同。

sentences.en: And the first couple of sections establish the fundamentals.
sentences.zh: 前几款确立了基本原则。

sentences.en: What are the qualifications for a member of the House?
sentences.zh: 众议院议员的资格是什么？

sentences.en: Who can be a senator?
sentences.zh: 谁可以成为参议员？

sentences.en: How can they be elected?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何选举产生的？

sentences.en: Now, who sets the rules that govern Congress?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁来制定管理国会的规则呢？

sentences.en: Congress does.
sentences.zh: 是国会自己。

sentences.en: Article 1 is also very clear about how lawmaking works.
sentences.zh: 第一条对于立法程序也写得非常清楚。

sentences.en: Our national bicameral legislature, that's the House and the Senate, is supposed to draft bills and then present these bills to the president for their approval or veto.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家两院制立法机构，也就是众议院和参议院，负责起草法案，然后提交给总统批准或否决。

sentences.en: Now, the big part of Congress's authority comes from Section 8.
sentences.zh: 国会权力的很大一部分来自第八款。

sentences.en: And those are the powers that Congress has.
sentences.zh: 这些就是国会拥有的权力。

sentences.en: Broad but specific powers in Article 1, like the power to spend money to tax and to regulate interstate commerce.
sentences.zh: 第一条中广泛但具体的权力，比如征税、支出以及监管州际贸易的权力。

sentences.en: So the purpose of Article 1 is both to recognize the enormous power of Congress,
sentences.zh: 所以第一条的目的既是为了承认国会的巨大权力，

sentences.en: but at the same time to reflect the concerns of the founders that there be clear limits on what a national legislative body can do.
sentences.zh: 同时也反映了开国元勋们的担忧，即必须对国家立法机构的职权范围进行明确限制。

sentences.en: So for most people, I think the words Article 1 don't have much significance in their daily lives, but it really is the how and the why of Congress.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，我认为“第一条”这个词在日常生活中没什么意义，但它确实是国会运作的原理和缘由。

sentences.en: And many of the things folks might be reading about today, from the massive increase in funding for ICE or the freezing of federal money for cancer research or foreign aid,
sentences.zh: 今天人们阅读的许多内容，从大幅增加移民及海关执法局（ICE）的资金，到冻结联邦癌症研究经费或对外援助，

sentences.en: These are happening not just because President Trump wanted them to happen, but because of the actions or inactions of Congress itself.
sentences.zh: 这些事情的发生不仅是因为特朗普总统想要它们发生，更是因为国会自身的作为或不作为。

sentences.en: That's the short summary.
sentences.zh: 这就是简要总结。

sentences.en: So, Representative Davis, you've been serving Kansas' third congressional district since 2019.
sentences.zh: 那么，戴维斯议员，您自2019年起就一直代表堪萨斯州第三国会选区。

sentences.en: And I'm so curious.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇。

sentences.en: So when you get elected, do you read and scrutinize Article 1 in a different way?
sentences.zh: 当您当选后，您阅读和审视第一条的方式是否有所不同？

sentences.en: Because, like, James Madison never wrote about my job, but your employee manual was written on stretched animal skin 250 years ago.
sentences.zh: 因为詹姆斯·麦迪逊从未写过关于我这份工作的说明，但您的员工手册是在250年前写在动物皮上的。

sentences.en: So when you first got elected, how did the Constitution change for you?
sentences.zh: 所以当您刚当选时，宪法对您来说有什么改变吗？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know what it's like for people who aren't lawyers when they come to Congress.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道非法律背景的人进入国会时是什么感觉。

sentences.en: But the first time I really thought about the impact of the Constitution, not just Article 1, but, like, as a whole document,
sentences.zh: 但我第一次真正思考宪法的影响，不仅仅是第一条，而是作为一份完整的文件，

sentences.en: was both when I was in law school and when I was practicing law,
sentences.zh: 是在我读法学院和从事法律工作的时候，

sentences.en: because I practiced law at the intersection of federal Indian law and corporate transactional and financing law.
sentences.zh: 因为我从事的是联邦印第安法律与企业交易及融资法律交叉领域的工作。

sentences.en: The most common of intersections.
sentences.zh: 最常见的交叉领域。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, there's at least 20 of us.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们至少有20个人。

sentences.en: No, just kidding.
sentences.zh: 不，开个玩笑。

sentences.en: And now they're actually, when I first was, when I was a baby lawyer, I think there weren't as many people practicing at that intersection, but there definitely are more now.
sentences.zh: 其实，当我刚入行做律师时，在这个交叉领域工作的人并不多，但现在确实多了起来。

sentences.en: But the reason I say that I had,
sentences.zh: 我之所以说我之前已经思考过这个问题，

sentences.en: I was already thinking a bit about that is because Congress has plenary power over the relationship between tribal governments and the federal government.
sentences.zh: 是因为国会对部落政府与联邦政府之间的关系拥有全权。

sentences.en: And that's part of the Interstate Commerce Clause, or sometimes what they call the Indian Commerce Clause.
sentences.zh: 这是州际贸易条款的一部分，有时也被称为“印第安贸易条款”。

sentences.en: But when I got elected, even though I had already spent so much time thinking about Congress's powers,
sentences.zh: 但当我当选后，尽管我已经花了很多时间思考国会的权力，

sentences.en: which powers have been vested in Congress with what was retained by the states,
sentences.zh: 思考哪些权力被授予了国会，哪些权力由各州保留，

sentences.en: what carries over when it comes to tribes and federally recognized tribes and the federal government, it did definitely take on a new meaning when I started this job.
sentences.zh: 以及在涉及部落、联邦承认的部落和联邦政府时，哪些权力会延续，当我开始这份工作时，它确实有了新的意义。

sentences.en: Because, well, one, just personally, as a Native American in this country, who I'm Ho-Chunk from Wisconsin, which is a federally recognized tribe,
sentences.zh: 因为，首先，作为这个国家的一名美洲原住民，我来自威斯康星州的霍昌克部落，这是一个联邦承认的部落，

sentences.en: it meant that my own personal relationship to my tribe and my relationship to all of Indian country was different.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我个人与我的部落以及我与整个印第安地区的关系变得不同了。

sentences.en: And so, there was like a personal thing, and then there's just the impact of knowing that for each of the members, we each represent somewhere around 700,000 people,
sentences.zh: 所以，既有个人层面的因素，也有作为议员的责任感，我们每个人大约代表70万人，

sentences.en: a little more in some places, a little less in others.
sentences.zh: 有些地方多一点，有些地方少一点。

sentences.en: And most people are not going to be familiar with Article 1, most people are not going to be familiar with federalism and states' rights and the delineation of those things.
sentences.zh: 大多数人不会熟悉第一条，大多数人也不会熟悉联邦制、州权以及这些权力的界定。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, I mean, it really did take on a whole different meaning, because not only was I doing the tasks, as you said, that are laid out, you know, meeting the qualification,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，它确实有了完全不同的意义，因为我不仅是在执行你所说的那些任务，比如满足资格要求，

sentences.en: but then actually, like, performing the tasks of a member of Congress.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上是在履行国会议员的职责。

sentences.en: I'm also, like, I'm the person who has to be most responsible in all of the Kansas Third for making sure that I'm adhering to the things that are in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 我还是堪萨斯州第三选区最需要确保遵守宪法规定的人。

sentences.en: I mean, that's such an interesting point, because, you know, when you look at the lawmaking part of Article 1, it seems pretty straightforward, right?
sentences.zh: 这真是一个有趣的观点，因为当你审视第一条中的立法部分时，它看起来相当直观，对吧？

sentences.en: It's just the House and the Senate get together, and they pass something, and then the president decides to do something.
sentences.zh: 就是众议院和参议院聚在一起，通过某项法案，然后总统决定做点什么。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But what I'd love to know is, you know, what's a common misconception do you think people have?
sentences.zh: 但我很想知道，你认为人们常见的误解是什么？

sentences.en: Like, there's probably a lot there that's not mentioned in the Constitution, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，宪法中肯定有很多没提到的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: So, what is it that we should know about that's actually hard or unknown about lawmaking?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于立法，有哪些是我们应该知道的、实际上很困难或鲜为人知的事情？

sentences.en: Um, I mean, one of the things, and actually, I was just, I was just mentioning this to someone on my team.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中之一，其实我刚才正和团队里的人提到这个。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, I wonder if it's going to come up, my view on, you know, that when people are running for president,
sentences.zh: 我在想，人们在竞选总统时，或者在任总统时，是否会谈到我的观点，

sentences.en: or are actually are the sitting president, often the president or presidential candidates will say something to the effect of,
sentences.zh: 通常总统或总统候选人会说类似这样的话：

sentences.en: when I, when I passed this law, when I wrote this law, I'm going to pass a law that does X.
sentences.zh: “当我通过这项法律时，当我撰写这项法律时，我将通过一项法律来做某事。”

sentences.en: Like, usually, you know, when they're making campaign promises, they'll say, I'm going to pass a law that does X.
sentences.zh: 通常，当他们做出竞选承诺时，他们会说：“我将通过一项法律来做某事。”

sentences.en: And it's like, I mean, you'll sign it.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，嗯，你会签署它。

sentences.en: But it's actually the Congress and the Senate that passed the laws.
sentences.zh: 但实际上是国会和参议院通过了法律。

sentences.en: It takes effect because the president signs it and it, you know, it is their bills and then they become a law once the president signs it.
sentences.zh: 它之所以生效是因为总统签署了它，这是他们的法案，一旦总统签署就成了法律。

sentences.en: But, but it really is like a much longer negotiation process in the House and then in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 但它确实是一个在众议院和参议院中漫长的谈判过程。

sentences.en: And then when the two have to come together and go into conference is what it's called, when the two pass bills that are substantially similar, but not exactly the same,
sentences.zh: 当两者必须走到一起并进入所谓的“协商会议”时，也就是当两者通过的法案基本相似但不完全相同时，

sentences.en: and they have to work out the differences.
sentences.zh: 他们必须解决分歧。

sentences.en: I just think that one, there's a lot more steps than most people probably imagine.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为，这比大多数人想象的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And then, because there's nothing in here about committees.
sentences.zh: 而且，宪法里根本没有提到委员会。

sentences.en: You know, there are committees of jurisdiction for each piece of legislation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每一项立法都有管辖委员会。

sentences.en: And so that there's like layers much deeper than the broad parameters that are set out by the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 所以这比宪法设定的广泛参数要深得多。

sentences.en: And the president doesn't, doesn't write the legislation, the Congress does.
sentences.zh: 而且总统并不撰写立法，国会才撰写。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: So when you first start, how do you learn how to do that?
sentences.zh: 那么当你刚开始时，你是如何学习如何做这些的？

sentences.en: What is the process like?
sentences.zh: 这个过程是怎样的？

sentences.en: Is there like a manual someone hands you on your first day?
sentences.zh: 第一天有人给你发手册吗？

sentences.en: Not exactly.
sentences.zh: 不完全是。

sentences.en: But there is, I'd say, two somewhat in-depth.
sentences.zh: 但我会说，有两个比较深入的环节。

sentences.en: It's weird to say in-depth because everything moves so quickly, but we have two orientations, basically.
sentences.zh: 说“深入”很奇怪，因为一切都进展得太快了，但我们基本上有两个入职培训。

sentences.en: There's an orientation.
sentences.zh: 有一个入职培训。

sentences.en: I guess there's three.
sentences.zh: 我想有三个。

sentences.en: One is optional.
sentences.zh: 一个是可选的。

sentences.en: I guess they're all optional, technically.
sentences.zh: 我想从技术上讲，它们都是可选的。

sentences.en: But, you know, the Congressional Research Service is, it's part of the Library of Congress.
sentences.zh: 但是，国会研究服务部是国会图书馆的一部分。

sentences.en: And they are this, like, amazing wealth of expertise.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有令人惊叹的专业知识储备。

sentences.en: There are experts on all matters that the Congress might take up or look at.
sentences.zh: 他们是国会可能处理或关注的所有事项的专家。

sentences.en: And they host an orientation for members of Congress who are just starting.
sentences.zh: 他们为刚开始工作的国会议员举办入职培训。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what happens on the Senate side.
sentences.zh: 我不确定参议院那边发生了什么。

sentences.en: But for the House, the Congressional Research Service hosts an orientation.
sentences.zh: 但对于众议院，国会研究服务部会举办入职培训。

sentences.en: And they go over all kinds of stuff with us.
sentences.zh: 他们会和我们讨论各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: They'll go over various powers.
sentences.zh: 他们会讨论各种权力。

sentences.en: They go over the fact that, you know, tax policy has to originate in the House.
sentences.zh: 他们会讨论税收政策必须起源于众议院这一事实。

sentences.en: They go over those types of things.
sentences.zh: 他们会讨论这类事情。

sentences.en: And then they also help, depending on which committee assignments you are hoping to get,
sentences.zh: 然后他们也会根据你希望获得的委员会分配，

sentences.en: they'll help with, like, jurisdictional.
sentences.zh: 提供管辖权方面的帮助。

sentences.en: Is this okay, how nerdy I'm getting?
sentences.zh: 我表现得这么书呆子气，没关系吧？

sentences.en: I feel like that's, okay.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这没问题。

sentences.en: This is exactly what is supposed to be in this moment.
sentences.zh: 这正是此刻应该有的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: That's one of them.
sentences.zh: 这是其中之一。

sentences.en: So the Congressional Research Service hosts something that really does help with some of
sentences.zh: 所以国会研究服务部举办的活动确实有助于我们处理一些

sentences.en: the substantive policy and committee work that we might be doing.
sentences.zh: 实质性的政策和委员会工作。

sentences.en: There's also an orientation that happens, like, in the building at the House.
sentences.zh: 还有一个入职培训是在众议院大楼里进行的。

sentences.en: And some of it is, you know, it's a federal job.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是，你知道，这是一份联邦工作。

sentences.en: So some of it is, like, here's your laptop.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些是，比如，这是你的笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: Here's your cell phone.
sentences.zh: 这是你的手机。

sentences.en: Sign the paper.
sentences.zh: 签个字。

sentences.en: That's not in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 那不在宪法里。

sentences.en: No, I know.
sentences.zh: 不，我知道。

sentences.en: And some of it is even, like, you know, we do our trainings.
sentences.zh: 其中一些甚至包括，你知道，我们进行的培训。

sentences.en: There's an ethics training.
sentences.zh: 有道德培训。

sentences.en: And then, you know, like, an office policy, making sure people aren't harassing each other
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，比如办公室政策，确保人们不会互相骚扰

sentences.en: type of training.
